text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

All newspapers lead with resignation of Hashim Mohamed Ali, executive chairman of Sukom Ninety Eight Bhd, the organiser of the 1998 Commonwealth Games to be hosted by Malaysia. Sukom was criticised over how it was promoting the games.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad has offered Malaysian expertise to Lebanon in the reconstruction of the country after a prolonged civil war.
-- Malacca Chief Minister Abu Zahar Isnin has asked state assemblymen and government officers to resign if they cannot work with him.

-- Another virus, identified as Enterovirus 71, has been detected in specimens from victims of the current viral outbreak in Sarawak. With the finding, there are now two viruses which could be linked to the deaths of 25 children since April 14.
-- Bumiputra developer Mustapha Kamal Abu Bakar is to inject property projects into second board counter Perfect Food Industries Bhd in a reverse takeover exercise, Mustapha said in an interview.
-- Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Monday announced further measures to spur the growth and development of Labuan as an international offshore financial centre.
-- The Registrar of Companies is proposing to amend provisions in the Companies Act 1965 relating to the appointment and resignation of company secretaries.
